# Ryan Whitaker – Thursday 5 November absence

## The code: UA

I've gone through each code against what Ryan actually told me in his 09:12 message, and the honest answer is that this is a **UA**.

- **SC** – He explicitly says "I wasn't ill yesterday." The team leader's SC code was based on a vague "not coming in" phone call; Ryan's own message corrects that. I can't leave it as SC.
- **DEP** – The definition is specific: *spouse or partner, child or parent, or someone who lives in the employee's household.* Ryan's sister is none of those. He lives alone; she is in Castleford. A niece's birth, while a family event, doesn't make the sister a qualifying dependant under the wording of the code. I can't stretch the definition to fit her, and I won't.
- **BRV** – No death. Not applicable.
- **UA** – "Any other absence that was not booked in advance." This is what it is. An unbooked absence that doesn't fall into any of the three specific categories.

So I will change the code from SC to **UA**.

## Why I'm not reaching for another code

I understand the temptation to call it DEP – "emergency, family, she needed help" – but the definition is closed. If I code a sister's premature labour as DEP, I'm rewriting the policy on a live file, and every future "my brother / my aunt / my friend" will expect the same treatment. The code exists to keep the boundary clear. I have to code what actually happened, not what would produce a kinder payroll line.

## What I will do before 12:00 (20 minutes)

1. **Add a free-text note to Ryan's UA entry.** The note doesn't affect payroll or probation, but it goes on his file, and the next person who reads this file should see the whole picture. I'll write something like:

   > *Employee confirms he was not ill. His sister (his emergency contact, Castleford) went into labour Wednesday night, two weeks early. Father of the baby works offshore and could not get back in time; the grandmother lives in Aberdeen. Ryan drove his sister to Pinderfields and stayed with her and the newborn through the night. He rang his team leader (Gary) at 05:40 for his 06:00 shift. Niece born 06:10, both well. Ryan acknowledges he is on probation and apologises. Circumstances are compassionate and exceptional; flag for management review.*

2. **Email the HR Manager immediately**, even though she is not in on Fridays. Subject line: **URGENT – Ryan Whitaker (Packing) – second UA will trigger auto-termination at 12:00 payroll run – please review before notice period runs.** I'll attach or summarise Ryan's message and the note. She works Monday to Thursday, so she will see it first thing Monday, but I want the flag in her inbox before she returns, not in a general Friday pile.

3. **Email the team leader (Gary) and the HR team**, same urgency, same content. Gary is on the floor until 14:00 and reads email after his shift, so he will see it this evening. The HR team may be in today and able to see it sooner. I'm not asking them to change the code – the code is what it is – I'm asking them to **review the automatic termination before the one-week notice expires**.

4. **Email Ryan himself.** A short, plain message: I've received his message, I've logged what he's told me, I'm flagging the probation consequence with management, and I'll let him know the outcome. I won't promise a result. I also won't pretend the code isn't what it is. But he should not be waiting in silence for a termination letter to arrive.

## Why the outcome is still fixable

The payroll system produces the letter at 12:00 and it is "sent out on the same day," but the letter ends his employment **with one week's notice**. That gives roughly until the following Friday for the HR Manager to read the file, see the note, read Ryan's message, and withdraw the notice. One week is not a lot, but it is a window. The team leader can also speak to Gary on the floor after 14:00 and confirm the 05:40 call went to him.

## What I will not do

- I will not code it DEP or SC to protect him. That misrepresents his absence and corrupts the record for his file, payroll, and any future reference.
- I will not delay submitting the list to "wait for the HR Manager." The other four entries (Leanne, Mohammed, Karen, Paul) need to hit payroll this week, and Mohammed's message means I should also check his code – his school-shut / no-one-to-look-after-his-daughter message reads more like DEP than SC, but I'll deal with that in the same pass.
- I will not unilaterally "waive" the second-UA rule. That's not in my remit. I can flag it; I can't overrule it.

## In short

The code is UA, the note carries the full compassionate context, and the urgent emails make sure the right human sees it before the one-week notice period is up. The system does what the system does at 12:00; my job is to make sure the human who can fix it knows, and knows fast, and has the evidence in front of them on Monday morning.
